rules.title: Package declaration header
rules.statement: A compilation unit begins with zero or more inner doc-comments (`//!`, `/*! */`) and inner attributes (`#![...]`), then `package NAME ('.' IDENT)* ';'`. The dotted path names the package to arbitrary depth (first component = NAME, remaining = PATH_PARTS). After the package line come zero-or-more use-declarations, then zero-or-more items.
rules.divergence: Rust has no `package` header; module identity comes from the file path plus `mod` items. Logos requires an explicit `package a.b.c;` line naming the full dotted package path.

rules.title: Plain use declaration
rules.statement: `[pub] use pkg ('.' IDENT)* ';'` brings a dotted package path into scope; `pub use` re-exports it. Path components after the head use a leading-dot separator (`path_dot_ident <- '.' IDENT`, with a negative lookahead against a following `.{` so the last component before a variant-shorthand brace-list is left for that alternative).

rules.title: Enum-variant bare-name import
rules.statement: `use pkg.Path.Type.{V1, V2, ...};` brings the named variants of enum `Type` into bare (unqualified) scope; trailing comma allowed. The last dotted component before `.{...}` is the enum type name.

rules.title: use with explicit source module
rules.statement: `[pub] use pkg ('.' IDENT)* IDENT use_module ';'` imports `pkg.path` from a named module; the from-bearing alternative is tried first (PEG ordered choice) and is unambiguous because a bare IDENT can only appear there as the contextual `from` keyword (`path_dot_ident` requires a leading `.`, so it never consumes it). `use_module` is a bare IDENT or a quoted STRING (for hyphenated module ids; sema strips the quotes).
rules.divergence: no Rust analog; disambiguates when more than one module could supply the same dotted path.

rules.title: Module item alternatives
rules.statement: A module item is one of: doc-comment (line/block, inner/outer), template decl, annotation, const/type-alias def, enum def (pub/plain), datatype def/instantiation (pub/plain), trait instance (pub/plain), struct unit/instantiation/def (pub/plain), explicit-instantiation decl (pub/plain), item-position metacall, resource decl, fn-macro item invocation, schema/schema-enum def (pub/plain), union def (pub/plain), trait def (pub/plain), impl block, extern block, extern fn def, or fn def (pub/plain).

rules.title: Outer line doc-comment binds to next item
rules.statement: An outer line doc-comment (`///`, DOC_LINE token) is captured as a DOC_LINE_LIT node sitting in the item/member stream; consecutive DOC_LINE_LIT siblings accumulate and the joined text attaches to the next real item.

rules.title: Outer block doc-comment
rules.statement: An outer block doc-comment `/** ... */` (DOC_BLOCK token) is captured as DOC_BLOCK_LIT with the same next-item-binding role as line doc-comments; the `/**`/`*/` envelope and each line's leading `*` indent are stripped and the lines joined with `\n`.

rules.title: Inner doc-comments form the enclosing module's doc summary
rules.statement: An inner doc-comment — `//!` (DOC_INNER) or `/*! ... */` (DOC_BLOCK_INNER) — never attaches to a specific item; instead it accumulates into the enclosing module's inner-doc summary (module_inner_doc). Both may appear, interleaved with inner attributes, before the `package` line.

rules.title: Doc-comment interleaved with struct/trait/impl members
rules.statement: Body-element slots admit either a real member or a doc-comment via `X_or_doc <- doc_line_decl / doc_block_decl / X` (X = field/method/trait_method/impl_item). Because the grammar is greedy with no lookahead, a doc-comment that visually precedes the FIRST method inside a body is captured by the preceding fields (or member) list rather than the methods list; sema carries any trailing doc-comment entries from that capture over into the methods iteration so "doc binds to the next member" holds despite the split capture.

rules.title: Item-position fn-macro invocation
rules.statement: `IDENT ! { ... }` at item position invokes a function-like macro whose body is captured as raw text (RAW_GROUP_BRACE); brace delimiter only at item position (parens/brackets stay reserved for expression position). The callee resolves through the item-splice pipeline (returns an item list).

rules.title: Named resource item declaration
rules.statement: `resource NAME = CALLEE!{ body };` desugars to the same FN_MACRO_CALL_ITEM node as an item-position fn-macro, but the left-hand NAME rides in the (otherwise-unused) NAME slot: sema passes it to the `#[token_macro]` callee as a second `str` arg so the emitted item is named by NAME, not by a `fn <name>` header inside body. A parameterized form `resource NAME = CALLEE!(PARAMS){ body };` additionally captures the parenthesized list as balanced raw source text (PARAMS), passed as a third arg; the callee re-emits it verbatim as the generated fn's real parameter list, so PARAMS is parsed and type-checked when that fn is compiled. The parameterized alternative is tried first (ordered choice; the extra paren group makes it strictly more specific, so plain `resource N = h!{ ... }` is unaffected).
rules.divergence: no Rust equivalent (ADR 0012 §6 named resource-macro item).

rules.title: Item-position metacall statement
rules.statement: `metacall <call_expr> ;` at item (module top-level) position invokes a metacall whose callee returns a `QuoteItemBlob`; the driver runs the JIT'd thunk, which splices the returned items into the enclosing program.

rules.title: Explicit instantiation root-pin
rules.statement: `[pub] instantiate <type_ref> ;` materializes the named generic instance as a monomorphization root: all its inherent and trait methods become roots, transitively pulling everything they call. `pub instantiate` additionally marks the instance as part of the package's public API surface (lib-site re-export).
rules.divergence: No Rust equivalent; analog of C++ `template class Foo<int>;`.

rules.title: Template declaration
rules.statement: `template <item>` wraps a struct/enum/datatype/trait/impl/fn declaration as inert data (an AST blob) rather than a real binding; the inner names are never registered by sema, so referencing the template as a type yields the ordinary unknown-type diagnostic. Templates are consumed later by metafunctions via apply/metacall.
examples: template struct Pair<A,B> { a: A, b: B }

rules.title: Outer attribute forms
rules.statement: An attribute is `#[ NAME (args) ]`, `#[ NAME = val ]`, or `#[ NAME ]`. The `= val` form admits an enum-literal value `IDENT::IDENT` or an integer.

rules.title: Inner attribute attaches to enclosing module
rules.statement: An inner attribute `#![ NAME (args) ]` / `#![ NAME = val ]` / `#![ NAME ]` (same payload shapes as an outer attribute) attaches to the enclosing module rather than to the following item; currently used only for `#![no_implicit_prelude]`.

rules.title: Attribute argument forms
rules.statement: Within an attribute's argument list, an argument is one of: `IDENT(args)` (nested call, ANNOT_CALL), `IDENT = lit` (key-value, ANNOT_KV), a bare literal (positional, ANNOT_POS), or a bare IDENT (legacy name-only form). A literal is an enum-variant ref `IDENT::IDENT`, a raw/normal string, a float, an integer, `true`/`false`, or a bracketed array of literals (`[lit, ...]`); lists allow a trailing comma.

rules.title: Module-level constant definition
rules.statement: A module constant is `[pub] let NAME: T = expr;` (non-generic, legacy form) or `[pub] const NAME [<T1,...>]: T = expr;`. `const` admits an optional type-parameter list absent from `let`: with type params, the RHS is a generic compile-time factory whose expression is templated and re-materialized (substituted) at each concrete use site. Both forms require an explicit type annotation and initializer and lower to the same CONST_DEF node.
rules.divergence: `let` accepted as a const keyword at module level; the generic `const NAME<...>` compile-time factory has no direct Rust analog.

rules.title: Module-level static definition
rules.statement: `[pub] static mut NAME: T = expr;` (STATIC_DEF, IS_MUT) declares a true mutable global with stable storage/address; `[pub] static NAME: T = expr;` (no IS_MUT) declares an immutable global with the same real-storage semantics — both distinct from `const`'s inline substitution (`&STATIC` identity holds). The `mut` alternative is matched before the non-mut alternative so `mut` is not swallowed as the binding's identifier.

rules.title: Type alias definition
rules.statement: `[pub] type NAME [<params>] = <type_ref>;` introduces a type alias, optionally generic via a type-parameter list.

rules.title: Enum definition
rules.statement: `[pub] enum NAME [<params>] [: backing_type] [where ...] { variants }` defines an enum with optional generic params, optional explicit backing integer type after `:`, optional variant list, and optional where-clause. A computed-name alternative `enum #(<expr>) [<params>] [: backing_type] { variants }` derives NAME_VAR from a compile-time expression instead of a literal IDENT; this alternative carries no where-clause slot (grammar restriction — NAME_VAR and WHERE occupy the same production slot).

rules.title: Enum variant shapes
rules.statement: A variant is one of: unit `Name`; tuple `Name(T, ...)`; variadic-tuple `Name(...T)` (a single variadic-typed payload field); struct-shape `Name { [pub] f: T, ... }` (fields optionally `pub`); empty struct-shape `Name {}`; or a discriminant-bearing `Name = <disc>`. `variant_list` allows leading doc-comments per variant and a trailing comma.

rules.title: Enum discriminant value forms
rules.statement: A variant discriminant `Name = D` may be: a bare (optionally negated) integer literal that is the complete value — matched only when NOT followed by a binary-operator token, else the value falls through to the general const-expr alternative; `metacall <block>`; a cross-enum reference `OtherEnum::Variant` with optional `as T` cast (the cast type is dropped — the discriminant's width is governed by the enclosing enum's own backing type/repr, not `T`); or a general constant expression evaluated via CTFE (the same `ctfe::eval_expr` channel metacall discriminants use).
rules.divergence: Cross-enum discriminant reference `OtherEnum::Variant` as a discriminant value has no Rust analog.

rules.title: Trait definition modifiers and supertraits
rules.statement: `[pub] [auto|unsafe] trait NAME [<params>] [: super (+ super)*] { items }` defines a trait; `auto` and `unsafe` are mutually-exclusive optional leading modifiers; the supertrait list after `:` is `+`-separated. Generic params, supertraits, both, or neither may be present, independently of the modifier.

rules.title: Trait method declarations
rules.statement: A trait method is `[unsafe] fn (NAME|new|null) [<params>] (params) [-> T] [where ...] (block | ';')`: a body-bearing form supplies a default implementation, a `;`-terminated form declares a required (abstract) method. `where` may follow the signature, before the block or the terminating `;`; on a default body it gates per-impl synthesis of that default (skipped for an impl where the bound doesn't hold for the impl's concrete type).
examples: fn max(self) -> Item where Item: Ord { ... }

rules.title: Associated type and const declarations in traits
rules.statement: A trait item may also be an associated type `type NAME [<params>] [: Bound (+ Bound)*] [= T] ;` (a non-empty `<params>` list makes it a GAT — generic associated type) or an associated const `const NAME: T [= expr] ;`, both with an optional default value/type.

rules.title: Impl block forms and targets
rules.statement: `[unsafe] impl [<impl_params>] [Trait [<args>] for] <target> [where ...] { items }` defines an impl; `Trait for Target` is a trait impl, omitting the trait is an inherent (standalone) impl. `<target>` ranges over: a simple named type (optionally with its own `<args>`), pointer type, reference type, bare unsized slice `[T]`, bare `dyn Trait`, tuple type `(A,B,...)`, or fn-pointer type `fn(A,B)->C`. An optional `where` clause may appear between the target and the opening brace.

rules.title: Negative impl
rules.statement: `impl [<params>] !Trait for <target> [where ...] {}` declares a negative impl asserting that `<target>` does NOT implement `Trait`; the grammar admits only the empty body `{}` (no impl items).

rules.title: Impl item kinds
rules.statement: An impl item is a method definition, an associated-type impl `type NAME [<params>] = T ;`, or an associated-const impl `const NAME: T = expr ;` (the value is required here, unlike the trait-side associated-const declaration where it's optional). Doc-comments may precede any impl item.
